builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CARE-FL: Federated Fine-Tuning of Multimodal LLMs in Resource-Constrained Edge Networks
summary: The method replaces heuristic or random client selection in federated LoRA fine-tuning of multimodal LLMs with a Double Deep Q-Learning selector using Q-value decomposition, constraint-aware epsilon-greedy subset selection, and an adaptive aggregation rule that can upweight the previous global model. It costs the engineering complexity of running an online RL selector and per-round utility estimation on top of the federated orchestration, plus the overhead of tracking latency and bandwidth feasibility each round. It can fail if the online-learned utilities misestimate client value under shifting data or system conditions, if the emulated wireless setting does not transfer to real deployments, or if the adaptive aggregation stalls convergence by overweighting stale models.
rationale: The reader operates a single 24 GB GPU or APIs with no federated edge fleet, so a client-selection framework for federated MLLM fine-tuning addresses an infrastructure scenario they do not have.
technique: Constrained RL client selection for federated LoRA fine-tuning

It costs the engineering complexity of running an online RL selector and per-round utility estimation on top of the federated orchestration, plus the overhead of tracking latency and bandwidth feasibility each round. It can fail if the online-learned utilities misestimate client value under shifting data or system conditions, if the emulated wireless setting does not transfer to real deployments, or if the adaptive aggregation stalls convergence by overweighting stale models.

Higher and more stable test accuracy than compared client-selection baselines on the CrisisMMD disaster-response task in emulated heterogeneous wireless edge environments, while satisfying per-round latency and bandwidth constraints; no numeric factor is reported in the abstract.
